mechanism_narrative: An increase in the federal funds rate by more than 0.5% in a month signals a tightening monetary policy, which typically leads to negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days as investors anticipate reduced economic activity and higher borrowing costs.
failure_condition: S&P 500 forward 20-day returns are positive in more than 60% of the instances where the federal funds rate increased by more than 0.5% in the previous month.

mechanism_narrative: A sharp increase in the unemployment rate by more than 0.5% in a month indicates a weakening labor market, which historically correlates with negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days due to concerns about future economic growth.
failure_condition: S&P 500 forward 20-day returns are positive in more than 60% of the instances where the unemployment rate increased by more than 0.5% in the previous month.

mechanism_narrative: A sustained decline in real GDP growth over two consecutive quarters signals a weakening demand environment, leading to negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 60 trading days as companies report lower earnings.
failure_condition: S&P 500 forward 60-day returns are positive in more than 60% of the instances where real GDP growth declined over two consecutive quarters.

mechanism_narrative: An increase in industrial production by more than 1% in a month signals a strengthening supply side, which typically leads to positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 5 trading days as investors anticipate increased economic activity and corporate earnings.
failure_condition: S&P 500 forward 5-day returns are negative in more than 40% of the instances where industrial production increased by more than 1% in the previous month.

mechanism_narrative: A simultaneous increase in housing starts and a decrease in retail sales signal a shift in consumer spending from goods to housing, which historically correlates with positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days as the market anticipates a robust housing sector.
candidate_trigger: HOUST increase > 5% and RSAFS decrease > 1% in 1 month
failure_condition: S&P 500 forward 20-day returns are negative in more than 60% of the instances where housing starts increased by more than 5% and retail sales decreased by more than 1% in the previous month.

mechanism_narrative: A decrease in nonfarm payrolls by more than 100,000 in a month indicates a weakening labor market, which typically leads to negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days as investors anticipate reduced consumer spending and economic growth.
failure_condition: S&P 500 forward 20-day returns are positive in more than 60% of the instances where nonfarm payrolls decreased by more than 100,000 in the previous month.

mechanism_narrative: A sustained increase in the Consumer Price Index (CPI) over two consecutive months signals inflationary pressure, which typically leads to negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 60 trading days as the market anticipates tighter monetary policy and reduced consumer purchasing power.
failure_condition: S&P 500 forward 60-day returns are positive in more than 60% of the instances where the CPI increased over two consecutive months.

mechanism_narrative: A simultaneous increase in real GDP and a decrease in the unemployment rate signal a strengthening economy, which historically correlates with positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 60 trading days as the market anticipates increased corporate earnings and consumer spending.
candidate_trigger: GDPC1 increase > 0.5% and UNRATE decrease > 0.3% in 1 quarter
failure_condition: S&P 500 forward 60-day returns are negative in more than 40% of the instances where real GDP increased by more than 0.5% and the unemployment rate decreased by more than 0.3% in the previous quarter.
